title: Cache Invalidation
description: Master cache invalidation patterns with queryClient.invalidateQueries to keep server state in sync.

data.text: After a mutation, the server state has changed but the React Query cache still holds the old data. Invalidation tells React Query which queries are now stale and should be refetched. Without invalidation, users see outdated data after writes.

items: invalidateQueries: Marks matching queries as stale and refetches them.
invalidateQueries({ exact: true }): Only matches the exact query key.
setQueryData: Manually update cache without refetching.
setQueriesData: Update multiple matching queries at once.
removeQueries: Delete queries from cache entirely.
data.title: Methods
Invalidating after mutation
data.content: Invalidate the todos query after adding a new one.

data.text: Use precise query keys to avoid refetching unrelated data. If you have paginated todos, invalidate only the affected page or use `invalidateQueries` with a predicate function.

data.title: Selective invalidation with predicate
data.content: Use a predicate for fine-grained control.

data.text: Over-invalidation causes unnecessary network requests. Under-invalidation causes stale data. Aim for the minimum invalidation scope that keeps data fresh.
data.title: Balance
Cache Invalidation Key Points
points: Invalidation marks queries as stale after mutations.
Use exact matching for precise control.
setQueryData enables optimistic updates without refetching.
Avoid over-invalidation to reduce network load.
data.takeaway: Cache invalidation is the bridge between mutations and fresh data.
